chunks: Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Ruba'i ibn Abdallah, from Abi Basir, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'They took their rabbis and monks as lords besides Allah,' he said: By Allah, they did not fast for them nor did they pray to them, but they made permissible for them the prohibited and prohibited for them the permissible, so they followed them.
ai.seo_question: How did the rabbis and monks become 'lords' besides God according to Shia interpretation?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the Quranic verse (9:31) regarding how Jews and Christians took their scholars as lords besides God. The Imam clarifies that it was not through their physical worship of the scholars, but through the scholars' authority to declare things halal (permissible) and haram (forbidden), which the people then followed as if it were divine law.
